r: There shall be a President of India
The **executive power of the Union is vested in the President**, exercised **either directly or through officers subordinate to him** (Ministers included) in accordance with the Constitution
**Supreme Command** of the Defence Forces vests in the President; its exercise **regulated by law**
Nothing in Art. 53 **prevents Parliament from conferring by law functions on authorities other than the President**
**Appointing the PM** – an **executive power** of the President
**Nominal / constitutional head**; **Head of State**, not Head of Government; **First Citizen**; **Rank 1** in the Order of Precedence; part of Parliament (**Art. 79**)
The **Council of Ministers** headed by the **PM** (**Art. 74(1)**), collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha – the mark of **parliamentary democracy**
All executive action is taken **in the President's name**
All **contracts** in exercise of the Union's executive power are **expressed to be made by the President** (for a State, by the Governor)
Every UT is administered by the **President**, through an **Administrator / Lieutenant Governor** appointed by him
A **Union Territory** in the First Schedule; the **69th Amendment, 1991** made it the **National Capital Territory** – **Art. 239AA**: Legislative Assembly + Council of Ministers
In **March 2010** the **MHA** ordered PCAs for the **Union Territories** (following Prakash Singh, 2006); States set up their own
**Art. 371-like safeguards** instead of the Sixth Schedule (Jul); a **sui generis** elected body (Sep)

**Governor** entrusts State functions **with the Union's consent** (7th Amendment, 1956)
Ensure **compliance with Union laws and existing laws**; Union may direct
State executive power must **not impede or prejudice** the Union's executive power
**Means of communication of national/military importance; protection of railways**
President may hold the State cannot be run per the Constitution → opens **Art. 356**
